purpose: Token-id probes for a BERT WordPiece tokenizer, checked against Hugging Face (results/tokenizer-ids.json, generated by reference/tokenizer_ids.py). The first ten come from texts.json so this set and the cosine comparison cover the same inputs.

probes.text: benchmark test sentence for embedding generation
how do lighthouse keepers wind the clockwork
The QUICK brown fox — didn't jump over the lazy dog?!
Café crème brûlée in São Paulo, naïve résumé
東京タワーの夜景 🚀 is beautiful

Lighthouses were once staffed by keepers who trimmed wicks, wound clockwork, and logged every passing ship through long winter nights. Automation arrived gradually: electric lamps replaced oil, rotating lenses were driven by motors instead of weights, and remote monitoring made resident crews unnecessary. Many towers now serve as museums, while their modern successors are small solar-powered beacons mounted on steel frames. Mariners still rely on the characteristic flash pattern of each light to fix their position when satellite navigation fails, which is why authorities publish detailed light lists every year.

supplementary-plane Cf between in-vocabulary text; the only probe that distinguishes Rune iteration from per-char, since flag_tag lands on [UNK] either way
Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers BertTokenizer lowercases before matching special tokens, so a lowercase literal [cls] in user text becomes the special token; Hugging Face only recognises [CLS]

Hugging Face's NFD splits Hangul syllables into conjoining jamo, which are in the vocabulary; Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers BertTokenizer with default options leaves the syllables whole and each word becomes [UNK]
